Hi Tom / EdgeFin team,

Great to chat today 	6 thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call on the SLO/benchmarking work so we can align on a reproducible methodology: 

- SLO targets discussed: P95 latency <= 150ms for 512-token responses, tail P99 <= 300ms.
- Throughput/concurrency: baseline target 200 concurrent streams (streaming enabled) with sustained throughput of ~250 requests/minute per cluster during peak.
- Streaming: long-poll streaming for partial tokens required (client uses server-sent events).
- Evaluation: you requested an apples-to-apples run against our runtime for your prompt set and prompt variants; reproducible harness and measurement definitions are critical.

Next steps (proposed):
1) You share the prompt set + any golden references and the preferred test dataset (we can accept S3 or Drive link).
2) We exchange a short benchmark spec (attached: redwood-benchmark-guidance-v1.pdf) that defines measurement windows, concurrency patterns, warmup behavior, and logging we need.
3) Run a representative pilot (2-4 hours) with both streaming and non-streaming variants.
4) Share raw logs + aggregated metrics (latency histograms, error rates, token counts).

Attaching our initial guidance doc (redwood-benchmark-guidance-v1.pdf) and a sample evaluation harness spec link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cEdgeFinBench

Can you send the prompt set and confirm the sample window you'd like us to run (dates/timezone)? We're proposing Wed-Thu next week (US PST mornings) for the pilot.

Thanks,

- We typically run 30-minute windows per configuration with 10-minute warmup; for the pilot we can extend to 2 hours to get stable tails.

Perfect 	6 thanks for the prompt set and the S3 location. A couple quick clarifying questions so our measurements align with yours: 

1) Measurement definitions: when you report P95/P99, do you include the time to first token (TTFT) only, or total time to last token (TTL) for the full response? For streaming we measure both TTFT and end-to-end TTL; please confirm which you primarily consider for SLO compliance.
2) Concurrency model: your note about 200 concurrent streams 	6 are those long-lived streaming connections (typical of SSE) or short-lived polling-style requests?
3) Tokenization: which tokenizer and model variant did you use when tagging token counts in the prompt set (helps us normalize token-rate measurements).

I've attached a short eval harness spec with the fields we log (eval-harness-spec.md). If you can confirm answers to the three questions above we can finalize the harness and schedule the pilot run.

Best,
Marissa

Subject: RE: Performance SLO qualification 	6 benchmark methodology exchange

Hi Tom / Marissa 	6 jumping in with the engineering perspective on measurement defs and harness settings: 

- Definitions: For streaming SLOs we recommend these primary metrics: TTFT (time to first token), steady-state token throughput (tokens/sec), TTL (time to last token) and tail latency (P95/P99 on per-request TTL). For our SLOs we evaluate based on P95 TTL but require TTFT not to exceed 100ms for interactive flows.
- Concurrency: When you say 200 concurrent streams we treat that as 200 long-lived SSE connections each receiving streamed tokens for the duration of the request. For load shaping we model a Poisson arrival process for short requests and sustained long-lived connections for the streaming cohort.
- Warmup & caching: Please note we run a 10-minute warmup and discard that window; KV-cache/prefix caching should be either disabled or explicitly described so runs are reproducible.
- Reproducibility: We'll ingest your promptset as-is (jsonl) but need to know the tokenizer model/version used to compute token counts. If you provide a small mapping (model -> tokenizer) we'll normalize.

I've attached a short note with recommended concurrency shaping and a sample locust config (aditya-concurrency-notes.txt). If you can confirm tokenizer details and whether KV-caching is on/off on your side, we can lock the run definitions.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com
[Attachment: aditya-concurrency-notes.txt (txt)]

Thanks 	6 quick answers: 
1) Our SLOs are based on TTL (end-to-end) for the official compliance check; we also track TTFT for UX. Use TTL P95/P99 for pass/fail.
2) Concurrency: yes, 200 are long-lived SSE streams.
3) Tokenizer: we use the HF tiktoken v0.4.2 tokenizer mapped to the model variant we listed in the promptset header (gptx-8k-v1).
4) KV-caching: off for the pilot (we want cold-start characteristics).

I'll upload pre-signed S3 links to s3://edgefin-perf/bench-v2/ by EOD and we can target Nov 30, 09:00-13:00 PST for the pilot window. Please confirm your cluster config (instance types / qps limits) you'll use so we can provision matching client-side generators.

Appreciate the quick turn, looking forward to the run.

\u007F
